abstract: Lazy quantum walks were presented by Andrew M. Childs to prove that the continuous-time quantum walk is a limit of the discrete-time quantum walk [Commun.Math.Phys.294,581-603(2010)]. In this paper, we discuss properties of lazy quantum walks. Our analysis shows that lazy quantum walks have $O(t^{n})$ order of the n-th moment of the corresponding probability distribution, which is the same as that for normal quantum walks. Also, the lazy quantum walk with DFT (Discrete Fourier Transform) coin operator has a similar probability distribution concentrated interval to that of the normal Hadamard quantum walk. Most importantly, we introduce the concepts of occupancy number and occupancy rate to measure the extent to which the walk has a (relatively) high probability at every position in its range. We conclude that lazy quantum walks have a higher occupancy rate than other walks such as normal quantum walks, classical walks and lazy classical walks.

specification.problem: Reconstruct, from the abstract alone, the discrete-time lazy quantum walk on the integer line with a three-dimensional coin acted on by the 3x3 Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) coin operator, its position probability distribution P_t(x), the n-th moment M_n(t) claimed to scale as O(t^n), and a measurable proxy for the paper's 'occupancy number' and 'occupancy rate' statistics.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction (chosen here as an assumption, since no experiment_scope was supplied): a lazy quantum walk on a finite line segment of 8 positions (3 position qubits, integer encoding x -> x+4 so that x in {-4,...,3}), coin register of 2 qubits embedding the 3 coin states {L,S,R} = {|00>,|01>,|10>} with |11> unused, DFT_3 coin embedded as F_3 (+) 1, t = 3 steps starting at x = 0 so that no boundary wrap-around occurs. Target quantities: P_t(x), M_n(t) for n = 1,2, and an occupancy number/rate computed with an assumed threshold rule. Outside scope: the proof that moments are O(t^n) in general, the continuous-time-limit construction of Childs, the comparison of concentration intervals with the Hadamard walk, the paper's exact definition of occupancy number/rate, and comparisons with classical and lazy classical walks.

symbols.meaning: walker position on the integer line
coin state index: 0 = move left, 1 = stay (lazy), 2 = move right
amplitude of the walker at position x with coin state c after t steps
primitive cube root of unity e^{2\pi i/3}
probability of finding the walker at position x after t steps
n-th moment of the position distribution after t steps
range of the walk after t steps (positions reachable with nonzero probability)
threshold defining a 'relatively high' probability (assumed definition)
occupancy number: count of positions in the range with probability at least the threshold (assumed definition)
occupancy rate: occupancy number divided by size of the range (assumed definition)

equations.label: Walker state and DFT coin operator
equations.description: The lazy walk uses a three-dimensional coin (left, stay, right); the coin operator is the 3x3 unitary DFT matrix.
equations.abstract_quote: the lazy quantum walk with DFT (Discrete Fourier Transform) coin operator
equations.justification: The abstract names the DFT coin; a lazy walk on the line has three coin outcomes, so the coin is the 3x3 DFT. The specific matrix (ordering of rows/columns, sign of the exponent) is the standard DFT and is not confirmed by the abstract.
assumptions: Coin dimension is 3 (left/stay/right) as in Childs' lazy walk on the line

equations.label: Lazy shift operator and one-step unitary
equations.latex: S=\sum_{x}\Big(|x-1\rangle\langle x|\otimes|0\rangle\langle 0|+|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes|1\rangle\langle 1|+|x+1\rangle\langle x|\otimes|2\rangle\langle 2|\Big),\qquad U=S\,(I\otimes F_3)
equations.description: Coin state 0 moves the walker left, state 1 leaves it in place (the 'lazy' option), state 2 moves it right; one step is coin followed by shift.
equations.justification: Standard definition of a three-state (lazy) discrete-time quantum walk on the line; the abstract only names lazy quantum walks and does not display this operator.
assumptions: Assignment of coin indices to directions is a convention
Coin is applied before the shift

equations.label: Evolution and position distribution
equations.description: Repeated application of the step unitary; the probability distribution over positions is obtained by tracing out the coin.
equations.justification: Standard discrete-time quantum walk evolution; required to define the distribution whose moments and occupancy the abstract discusses.

equations.label: n-th moment scaling
equations.description: The n-th moment of the lazy-walk position distribution grows at most as t^n, matching the ballistic scaling of ordinary (non-lazy) quantum walks.
equations.abstract_quote: lazy quantum walks have $O(t^{n})$ order of the n-th moment of the corresponding probability distribution, which is the same as that for normal quantum walks
equations.justification: Stated directly in the abstract; the definition of M_n(t) as the raw moment about x=0 is the standard one and is an interpretation.
assumptions: Moment taken about the origin (raw moment) rather than a central moment; the abstract does not specify
Asymptotic statement; not verifiable from the t=3 scoped instance

equations.label: Assumed occupancy number and occupancy rate
equations.description: A proposed operational definition: positions in the range whose probability is at least a 'relatively high' threshold are counted; the rate normalises by the range size. The threshold 1/|R_t| (the uniform-distribution value) is an assumption.
equations.justification: The abstract introduces occupancy number and occupancy rate as measures of 'the extent to which the walk has a (relatively) high probability at every position in its range' but gives no formula; this is a plausible proxy, explicitly not the paper's definition.
assumptions: Threshold choice \theta_t = 1/|R_t| is invented here for concreteness and may differ from the paper
Range defined as support of P_t; the paper may use the kinematic range \{-t,\dots,t\}

equations.label: Scoped instance: encoding and initial state
equations.description: Position stored as an unsigned 3-bit integer with offset 4; the 3-state coin is embedded in 2 qubits with |11> inert under the coin; walker starts at the origin in the 'stay' coin state and takes 3 steps (|x| <= 3, so no wrap-around occurs and the modular shift equals the integer shift).
equations.justification: Smallest explicit instance chosen for a later circuit stage; the abstract specifies no sizes, initial state, or encoding.
assumptions: Initial coin state |1> (stay) is a choice; symmetric superpositions are equally plausible
Shift implemented as modular increment/decrement on 3 qubits; exact for t <= 3 from x = 0
Coin state |11> never becomes populated because \tilde F and S act trivially on it and the initial state has no |11> component

registers.name: pos
registers.role: Position register storing x+4 as an unsigned integer (x in {-4,...,3}); qubit 0 is the least significant bit.

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Coin register embedding the three lazy-walk coin states: |00> = left, |01> = stay, |10> = right; |11> unused.

steps.description: Prepare the initial state: set pos to the encoding of x = 0 and coin to |01>.
Apply the embedded DFT coin \tilde F = F_3 (+) 1 to the coin register.
Apply the coin-conditioned shift: controlled on coin = |00> apply a modular decrement to pos, controlled on coin = |10> apply a modular increment to pos, do nothing for coin = |01>.
Repeat the coin and shift steps for a total of t = 3 iterations, realising U^t.
Measure the position register in the computational basis; repeat the whole circuit to estimate P_t(x).

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the 3 pos qubits (coin register may be discarded or measured and marginalised). Decode x = (measured integer) - 4. Repeat shots to estimate P_t(x) for t = 3.
specification.classical_postprocessing: From the estimated P_t(x): compute M_1(t) and M_2(t) via eq_4; determine the range R_t as the set of positions with (statistically) nonzero probability, and compute the assumed occupancy number N_occ(t) and occupancy rate rho_occ(t) via eq_5 with threshold theta_t = 1/|R_t|. Optionally compare with a classical lazy random walk (probabilities 1/3 left/stay/right) computed exactly.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was provided, so a single smallest instance (8 positions, 3 steps, origin start, 'stay' initial coin) was chosen as an assumption.
The coin is the 3x3 DFT with the standard phase convention; coin applied before shift; coin index-to-direction assignment is conventional.
Occupancy number/rate definitions in eq_5 are a proposed proxy, not the paper's definitions.
Moments are raw moments about the origin.
Finite register with modular arithmetic is exact for the chosen t because the walker never reaches the boundary.
missing_information: The paper's precise definitions of occupancy number and occupancy rate (threshold rule, definition of 'range').
The initial state (position and coin) used in the paper's analysis and comparisons.
Whether the 'lazy quantum walk' uses exactly the DFT_3 coin or Childs' parameterised lazy coin, and any laziness parameter.
Exact statement and proof of the O(t^n) moment result and the 'concentrated interval' comparison with the Hadamard walk.
Any numerical values (occupancy rates, step counts) reported in the paper for quantum, classical and lazy classical walks.
